profile.themes: Export Mix Shift to High-Margin Auto OEM; FX Tailwinds; Capacity Expansion in Existing Footprint

bull_bear.body: Focus on organic capacity expansion within existing footprint to minimize capex; evaluating global location for strategic de-risking; CSR initiatives (45k+ plants, education/health).
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Volatility in crude/PVC prices; Geopolitical tensions impacting freight/logistics (Middle East/Europe); Labor code cost inflation; Customer concentration in auto OEMs; FX reversal risk.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident on structural margin re-rating (25-30% vs historical 24-25%); Conservative on guiding specific quarterly numbers but firm on annual growth trajectories; Transparent on FX and labor code impacts.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: The margin jump to 31% is not just cyclical but structural due to the mix shift to auto exports (50% growth) which are dollar-priced and higher margin. The INR 3 Cr Q4 FX gain is small relative to the operational leverage gained from the export mix. Employee cost spike is a one-time regulatory adjustment (new labor codes) rather than aggressive hiring.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

business.body: Q4 Breakdown (Standalone): Export OEM INR 88 Cr; Auto OEM Domestic INR 55 Cr; Replacement INR 41 Cr; Footwear INR 48 Cr; Export General INR 21 Cr; Furnishing INR 5 Cr. Full Year Export Auto grew 50% to INR 290 Cr. PU business remains muted (FY26 rev INR 27 Cr).
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Raw material price volatility and logistics disruptions | Mayur Uniquoters Ltd | beneficiary | High | Company successfully passed on price hikes with a lag and benefited from dollar-denominated auto contracts; low-capex expansion improves ROCE profile. |
business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

latest_quarter.body: Q4 margin expansion driven by: 1) Higher export mix (42.5% of total, rising); 2) FX gains on dollar-denominated auto contracts; 3) Operating efficiency (OE) improvements; 4) Lower freight/maintenance costs. Raw material (PVC paste/Yarn) prices rose in March but availability is stable; price hikes passed to customers with 1-2 month lag.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Revenue Growth: Domestic 8-10%, Export 15-20% (Value terms). Margin: 25-30% EBITDA range expected. Order Inflow: Strong projections from existing auto platforms; Ford platform expansion ongoing. Capex: INR 50 Cr for new coating line in existing facility (commissioning by Dec 2026); INR 300 Cr reserved for future global location (Mexico/other).
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: No fixed order book; business runs on monthly volume projections from OEMs. Export auto OEM revenue for FY26 was INR 290 Cr vs INR 194 Cr in FY25 (+50%).
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Expansion of Ford platforms; penetration in European/US marine and furnishing segments; potential greenfield global plant (INR 300 Cr) to bypass tariffs/logistics.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Mayur Uniquoters delivered a blowout Q4FY26 with PAT up 73% YoY (standalone), driven by a structural shift toward high-margin automotive exports (up 50% YoY) and favorable FX realization. Management guides for sustained 25-30% EBITDA margins and ~15-20% export growth, underpinned by a low-capex capacity addition (INR 50 Cr) commissioning by year-end.

open.item: Buyback not yet decided/discussed; typically considered after final (year-end) results.
Guidance to maintain 25-26% margin, with potential 25-30% in long term given export mix and currency; not committing to sustained 30%.
Price hike taken for domestic footwear/open market in Q4; automotive price increase (from March RM rise) to reflect in Q1FY27, both RM cost and price impacts.
Ordered a coating line to be installed in existing facility (not South India), capex within ~INR50 crores, to be done by end of calendar year 2026.
Domestic value growth guidance of 8-10% for FY27 and next 2-3 years.
Export value growth guidance of 15-20% (up to 25%) for FY27 and coming years, automotive-led.
Export mix expected around 40-45% of revenue in FY27 (from 42.5% in FY26).
Global-location plant (Mexico or other country) capex ~INR300 crores still under evaluation; location not finalized.
New coating line to add ~5 lakh meters/month (4-6 range), increasing revenue by ~INR120-150 crores.
Targeting growth in general export (marine, furnishing) and new segments in Europe/USA beyond automotive; currency depreciation gives competitiveness.
EU-India FTA (zero duty, ~10-12 months to sign) expected to strongly help non-automotive/general export business; US remains first target market.

verdicts.item: 10% US tariff on India from April 2025 flagged; management states their material is not under US customs duty tariff category, no tariff impact currently.
verdicts.note: Arun: 'when the US tariff came, our general export business did not go down... the impact of the US duty is not visible in the overall year' — OEM unaffected, but the expected general-export uplift wa…

verdicts.item: Export OEM growth expected at least 15% this year and 15-20% next year, growing at least 15% for the next 3 years.
verdicts.note: Vinod: 'Auto exports for the current year INR290 Cr., and last year it was INR194 Cr... increased by about 50%'; Arun: 'our export growth is 35%.'

verdicts.item: Management planning to professionalize the organization; process ongoing.
verdicts.note: Q4FY26 call run by ED Mr. Arun Bagaria and the CFO (Chairman/MD Poddar not on the management panel) — professionalization progressing.

verdicts.item: Reaffirmed FY26 guidance of ~10-15% (12-15%) top-line growth.
verdicts.note: Arun: 'we registered a total growth of 15% in value.'

verdicts.item: Reaffirmed FY26 guidance of 15-20% bottom-line growth.
verdicts.note: Standalone Q4 PBT +70%, PAT +73% YoY with ~30% margins — FY26 bottom-line growth exceeded 15-20%. [±10% rule]

verdicts.item: Mexico plant postponed due to tariff confusion but intact; will proceed once tariff situation settles, not considering other location.
verdicts.note: Arun: 'it could be Mexico or some other country'; and instead of a fresh South India plant, 'we have found space in an existing facility' — contradicts 'not considering other location.'

verdicts.item: Auto OEM export unaffected by US tariff (Tier-1 supply via Mexico); no worry up to 25% tariff, but newly announced 50% tariff (from 27 Aug) on select items is a worry, needs analysis.
verdicts.note: Arun: 'our general export business did not go down... the impact of the US duty is not visible in the overall year' — auto OEM unaffected; general export uplift nullified by the duty.

verdicts.item: Working 6-8 months with big brands (Aditya Birla, Adidas) on footwear/leather goods/garments; trial orders started, full ramp expected in 1-2 years with better margins.
verdicts.note: Arun: 'we are definitely talking to a lot of brands. But business has not matured till now... approved us as a vendor. But no price commercial settlement has happened till now.'

verdicts.item: Won order from Ford for super models; supply to grow from ~10,000 yards to more than 100,000 yards in the next 2 years.
verdicts.note: Arun: 'our volume with Ford was very low. So, we have added more platforms on Ford business. The business has started increasing. But it will increase more in the coming months.'

verdicts.item: In discussions with Ford Motor in South Africa; discussion already started to add customers.
verdicts.note: Arun: 'we have added more platforms on Ford business. The business has started increasing' — Ford customer expanding (US market).

verdicts.item: Replacement market stagnant (3-4 OEMs down, design changes); no massive increase expected but slight improvement.
verdicts.note: Q4 breakup: 'Replacement INR41 crores' vs Q3 INR38.84 cr — continued slight improvement.

verdicts.item: Strategy to diversify across segments (automotive, footwear, leather goods, garments) and never depend on one customer; working with US Stellantis and expanding models.
verdicts.note: Arun: 'we are trying to enter into new segments also... growth in the marine... furnishing... other markets also in Europe and in the USA. So, we are working on all angles' — diversification ongoing, …
